title: 〜っけ
meaning: "was it ~?", "what was ~ again?" — checking a hazy memory.
simpleExplanation: Normally attaches to a past plain form even when you are asking about the present. It is casual, though 〜でしたっけ / 〜ましたっけ can be used politely.
whenUsed: Casual conversation when you half-remember something and want confirmation.
formation: Plain past + っけ (V-た / い-adj-かった / N・な-adj + だった + っけ)
Polite: 〜ましたっけ / 〜でしたっけ

branches.result: そんなに高かったっけ
branches.label: was it that expensive?

examples.ja: 明日の会議は何時からだっけ。
examples.reading: あしたのかいぎはなんじからだっけ。
examples.en: What time was tomorrow's meeting again?

examples.ja: あの人の名前、何だったっけ。
examples.reading: あのひとのなまえ、なんだったっけ。
examples.en: What was that person's name again?

examples.ja: 君も同じクラスだったっけ？
examples.reading: きみもおなじクラスだったっけ？
examples.en: Were you in the same class too?

examples.reading: あのひと、だれでしたっけ。

similarGrammar.difference: Confirmation of something you are fairly sure about. っけ signals you've forgotten.
Adds the explanatory ん: 何時に来るんだっけ.

commonMistakes.right: 会議は何時からだっけ？
commonMistakes.why: Nouns need だ (or だった) before っけ.

commonMistakes.wrong: 会議は何時からでしたっけ？(to a close friend, casual context)
commonMistakes.why: Not wrong, but でしたっけ is polite; match the register of the conversation.

commonMistakes.right: 彼は来るんだっけ？/ 来るんでしたっけ？
commonMistakes.why: Plain non-past verbs do not take っけ directly; add んだ.

usageNotes: Casual; uses past-tense forms even for present facts. Can be self-directed (talking to oneself). Not used with plain non-past + っけ except だっけ.
っけ often follows あれ / えっと, showing the speaker is searching memory.
jlptTips: A casual question with 何 / いつ / どこ and a blank at the end where the speaker seems to have forgotten = っけ.
Check the form: だっけ / だったっけ / たっけ. A plain dictionary verb + っけ is a wrong option.
In listening, っけ marks a speaker confirming a detail; the answer usually comes in the next line.
